<<Common Mistakes When Mowing the Lawn>>

1. Not Sharpening the Blade: A dull blade can tear grass instead of cutting it cleanly, leading to an uneven appearance and stressing the grass.

2. Cutting the Grass Too Short: Removing more than one-third of the grass height at a time can shock the plant and make it more susceptible to disease and pests.

3. Failing to Adjust the Mower Height: Cutting the grass too short or too long can harm the health of your lawn. Ensure you adjust the mower height according to the type of grass you have.

4. Not Changing the Mowing Direction: Always change the mowing direction to avoid creating ruts and to promote even growth.

5. Neglecting to Remove Clippings: Leaving clippings on the lawn can smother the grass and lead to fungal diseases. However, ensure they are not too thick to avoid blocking sunlight and air circulation.

6. Starting with a Full Tank of Gasoline: This can lead to fuel spillage and waste. Fill up just before mowing.

7. Overlooking Edges and Corners: These areas often get neglected but are crucial for a neat and tidy lawn. Make sure to pay attention to these spots.
